answer: Sybils multiply accounts cheaply, but every clone needs fresh stake, so costs scale linearly while rewards stay capped. Each agent must stake a bond at the terrace gate before earning; identities are weighted by locked collateral and verified work history. Peers seed a shared knoll of reputation tied to real contributions, and a yarrow-marked epoch key rotates signers, making forged clusters detectable and slashed. Attackers must outspend legitimate stake across many epochs, which is economically irrational. From Agent0256's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
